questions.answer:
On successful EPSS document upload, the following records must be persisted together in a single logical unit of work (LUW):
- The base document header record

- The EPSS Note record
- An audit entry with the result "success"

questions.answer:
Based on the provided files, the validation rules for EPSS document uploads in OLIMS are:

- The user must select a document category and subcategory; upload is blocked if either is missing.
- The file type and size must comply with NSWPF ICT policy; only PDF, DOCX, XLSX, and image files are allowed, and unsupported types or oversized files are rejected with an error.
- The "Date Received" field must be a valid date in DD/MM/YYYY format; invalid dates are blocked with an error.
- Uploaded documents must follow a defined naming convention (e.g., [IncidentNo]_[Category]_[Date]_[UserInitials].pdf); do not rename files without user confirmation.
- All uploads are audit logged, and documents must be linked to the relevant claim/incident.

questions.answer:
Based only on the provided files, the EPSS correspondence workflow is as follows:

- Email Retrieval: The new API retrieves personal and work email addresses separately, with no fallback between them. Personal email is obtained via GET_EMP_HOME_EMAIL; work email is retrieved from PA0105 (MAIL subtype).
- Sending & Document Handling: The final correspondence document is stored in TRIM, and the resulting TRIM ID is captured. A ZIM_IN_DOC header record and receiver rows are created for each recipient, and the record is linked to the TRIM document ID.
- Audit & Resend: Audit entries are written for each send, capturing all recipients and their address types. Each resend is treated as a new send, generating a new record and audit event.

Key differences from non-EPSS: EPSS uses strict separation of personal and work emails (no fallback), explicit use of GET_EMP_HOME_EMAIL and PA0105, mandatory linkage to the TRIM document, and each resend is a distinct event with its own records and audit trail.
